questions: Should words that start with '$' but contain whitespace inside them (e.g., due to tokenization quirks) be considered as a single word, or split further?
Is the '$' character required to be at the very start of a token as defined by whitespace separation, or can it appear after leading whitespace within a token?
Should the function treat words with mixed alphanumeric and special characters (e.g., '$a!b') as valid, or only if they contain at least one non-special character after the '$'?
Does 'special characters' refer strictly to string.punctuation, or include other non-alphanumeric symbols like Unicode punctuation?
Should the output DataFrame be sorted in any particular order (e.g., by frequency, alphabetically), or is any order acceptable as long as columns are correct?
If a word appears multiple times with different casing (e.g., '$Hello' vs '$hello'), should they be considered the same word (case-insensitive) or different?
Are words that start with '$' but are immediately followed by whitespace (i.e., standalone '$') considered valid, or ignored as entirely special characters?
Should the function strip or ignore leading/trailing punctuation from the word after the '$' before checking if it's entirely special characters?
